item.title: Smart Routing Framework for Urban Curbside Scanning: A Framework for Time‐Optimized and Spatially Representative Data Collection
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT Urban curbside monitoring requires routes that balance travel efficiency with representative sensing coverage. This study develops a reproducible GIS‐based routing framework for vehicle‐based residential curbside scanning. The framework integrates local‐residential target link identification, deterministic farthest point sampling, directed‐network routing, exact/MILP/GA benchmarking, Pareto‐based sensing route selection, and post‐routing diagnostics. It was evaluated across four Residential Parking Program zones in Edmonton, Canada, using four alternatives: fixed‐order baseline, Dijkstra nearest‐neighbor, exact/MILP/GA‐best, and sensing‐oriented routes. All alternatives met the 30‐min survey window requirement. The exact/MILP/GA‐best route minimized travel burden, averaging 5.86 km and 7.97 min across zones. The sensing‐oriented route increased the mean distance to 6.76 km but achieved the highest mean local‐residential target share (84.3%). Operational diagnostics showed that optimized routes reduced difficulty, repeated traversal, and turn burden relative to the fixed‐order baseline. The results demonstrate the value of multi‐criteria, sensing‐aware routing for scalable curbside inventory collection.

ABSTRACT

Urban curbside monitoring requires routes that balance travel efficiency with representative sensing coverage. This study develops a reproducible GIS-based routing framework for vehicle-based residential curbside scanning. The framework integrates local-residential target link identification, deterministic farthest point sampling, directed-network routing, exact/MILP/GA benchmarking, Pareto-based sensing route selection, and post-routing diagnostics. It was evaluated across four Residential Parking Program zones in Edmonton, Canada, using four alternatives: fixed-order baseline, Dijkstra nearest-neighbor, exact/MILP/GA-best, and sensing-oriented routes. All alternatives met the 30-min survey window requirement. The exact/MILP/GA-best route minimized travel burden, averaging 5.86 km and 7.97 min across zones. The sensing-oriented route increased the mean distance to 6.76 km but achieved the highest mean local-residential target share (84.3%). Operational diagnostics showed that optimized routes reduced difficulty, repeated traversal, and turn burden relative to the fixed-order baseline. The results demonstrate the value of multi-criteria, sensing-aware routing for scalable curbside inventory collection.

item.title: Scale Dependence of Landslide Exposure Variability Derived From Gridded Population Products Across Mainland China
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT Accurate population exposure estimates are needed for regional‐scale landslide exposure mapping, yet they can be strongly affected by the choice of gridded population datasets. This study evaluates dataset‐induced uncertainty in landslide population exposure estimates across mainland China. We quantified variability among population products in landslide exposure across mainland China by overlaying seven 2020 gridded population products with the rainfall‐induced landslide susceptibility map and compared exposure estimates across geomorphic, administrative, and basin‐based spatial units. The combined medium, high, and very high classes were used as the principal potential‐impact range, while the combined high and very high classes were analyzed as a stricter threshold. PopSE‐China, a 100 m population dataset constrained by China's seventh national census and high‐resolution geospatial covariates, was used as a census‐constrained local comparator, not as ground truth; agreement metrics therefore indicate relative consistency rather than accuracy. Exposure estimates varied substantially among the gridded population datasets. National exposed populations ranged from 201.0 to 276.1 million under the M+ scenario and from 88.6 to 150.1 million under the H+ scenario. Among the evaluated datasets, GPWv4 yielded the highest national exposure estimates, whereas PopSE‐China yielded the lowest, highlighting the substantial influence of population dataset selection on landslide exposure assessment. Spatially, exposed populations were concentrated primarily in the Southwestern Mountains (approximately 117 million) and the Southeastern Mountains (approximately 68.1 million). Scale‐dependent analysis further showed that the consistency of priority areas increased at finer spatial scales, with the mean Jaccard index of the top 10% priority counties under the M+ scenario reaching 0.801, compared with 0.693 at the basin scale. These findings support a data fitness‐for‐use perspective for selecting gridded population products in landslide exposure mapping and broader geospatial hazard assessment.

item.title: Reconstructing Gully Inlets Across Spatially Heterogeneous Urban Environments Using Street View Imagery: A Detection‐Interpolation Framework
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT Accurately characterizing the spatial heterogeneity of stormwater collection capacity is critical for reducing urban flood simulation uncertainties but is hindered by the scarcity of drainage infrastructure data. This study proposes a camera‐parameter‐free framework using public street‐view imagery for gully inlet mapping. To overcome the sampling instabilities of mainstream 1D centerline sampling (CLS), a 2D grid‐based sampling (GBS) strategy is proposed, alongside a localized median interpolation method to reconstruct data missing from environmental occlusions. Validation using ground‐truth GNSS data in Guangzhou demonstrates that by controlling the total gully inlet count at the street scale, this framework accurately captures macro‐scale spatial differentiation. It achieves low count deviations (−6.0% to 8.2%), significantly outperforming CLS (−46.9% to −33.7%). Inundation simulations further indicate that the reconstructed spatial patterns align highly with recorded flood points, correcting the significant runoff overestimation caused by CLS omissions. This study offers a novel and low‐cost paradigm for urban infrastructure spatial data acquisition.
item.content:encoded:
ABSTRACT

Accurately characterizing the spatial heterogeneity of stormwater collection capacity is critical for reducing urban flood simulation uncertainties but is hindered by the scarcity of drainage infrastructure data. This study proposes a camera-parameter-free framework using public street-view imagery for gully inlet mapping. To overcome the sampling instabilities of mainstream 1D centerline sampling (CLS), a 2D grid-based sampling (GBS) strategy is proposed, alongside a localized median interpolation method to reconstruct data missing from environmental occlusions. Validation using ground-truth GNSS data in Guangzhou demonstrates that by controlling the total gully inlet count at the street scale, this framework accurately captures macro-scale spatial differentiation. It achieves low count deviations (−6.0% to 8.2%), significantly outperforming CLS (−46.9% to −33.7%). Inundation simulations further indicate that the reconstructed spatial patterns align highly with recorded flood points, correcting the significant runoff overestimation caused by CLS omissions. This study offers a novel and low-cost paradigm for urban infrastructure spatial data acquisition.
